summary: The new src/lib/browser-execution/ module is architecturally sound (clean tier fallback chain, fail-open caching, deterministic-first policy matching phase_2's compiler, browser-safe imports that correctly avoid the prompt-compiler barrel) and its own 43 unit tests pass, but the diff breaks the TypeScript build: refactoring LLMUsage out of src/lib/llm-client.ts into the new src/lib/llm-pricing.ts left llm-client.ts with only a type re-export (`export type { LLMUsage } from "./llm-pricing"`) instead of an import, so llm-client.ts's ~10 internal function signatures that reference LLMUsage directly (callAnthropic, callOpenAICompatible, callGoogle, etc.) no longer resolve the name -- `bunx tsc --noEmit` fails with 11 TS2304 errors, all in this one core, widely-imported module. This is precisely the risk the worker's own PROGRESS.md flagged as unverified ("Full repo tsc/lint pass has NOT been run this session... Must run before merge") and it does not in fact pass. No .github/workflows/** files are touched. Reject until the missing `import type { LLMUsage } from "./llm-pricing"` (or equivalent) is added to llm-client.ts and a full tsc/lint pass is confirmed green.
issues: src/lib/llm-client.ts fails to compile: `export type { LLMUsage } from "./llm-pricing"` (line 72) only re-exports the type for external importers, it does not bind LLMUsage locally -- 11 `error TS2304: Cannot find name 'LLMUsage'` across the file's own function signatures (lines 76, 221, 277, 343, 377, 413, 468, 501, 528, 554, 609). Fix: add `import type { LLMUsage } from "./llm-pricing";` alongside the re-export.
Worker's own PROGRESS.md explicitly states a full repo tsc/lint pass was not run this session -- that gap is real and hides the build-breaking error above; must be run and green before merge.

Task's own remaining-work list (PROGRESS.md) also notes: no PR opened yet, VeriComposer.tsx integration not started, e2e/browser-execution.spec.ts Playwright proof not written, and phase_5 status in the claude-control repo's phase plan not updated -- none of these block a correctness verdict on their own, but confirm this is a partial/in-progress submission, not a complete one.
